newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, buyers' reserve.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, buyers' reserve.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices fell at the close after reacting to a lower Tokyo futures market and continued absence of consumer demand, dealers said.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board set market indicator price for October RSS1 buyer at 327.50 cents ($1.31) a kg, down half a cent from Monday. October SMR20 buyer ended a cent lower at 313.5 cents.
Trading houses offered the SMR20 at between 314-315 cents, SMR10 at 313-316, SMR5 at 326, SMR L at 353-356, SMR CV at 373-376 and drum latex at 247-248.
Sentiment remained soft, with Tokyo being the only lead.
"The market was just like yesterday...nothing happening," said a dealer.

Traders said demand has been rather slow after the jump in prices two weeks ago, prompted by a tight raw materials supply owing to rain. The Malaysian Metereological Services Department said it expected the weather to stay wet this week, although less rain was forecast.
The INRO five-day indicator fell to 252.08 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Sept 9 from 252.55 on Sept 6. The daily indicator fell to 250.32 from 251.44.
